descriptionChirho: Aramaic verb meaning to will, wish, or desire, used exclusively in Daniel for divine or royal volition. All four clusters share identical semantics across languages: Spanish quiere/quería/deseé (wants/wanted/desired), Arabic يَشَاءُ / أَرَدْتُ (wills / I wanted), Korean 원하시는 / 원했다 (the one who wills / desired), Hindi चाहता है / चाहा (wants / wanted), Swahili anapenda / nilitaka (likes / I wanted). The variation is purely inflectional (imperfect, participle, infinitive, perfect 1cs) with no semantic divergence.
